payments.nothingToPay: Nothing left to pay on this vendor’s bills.

budgets.nothingYetBody: Add amounts to the plan, or post some income and expenses.
budgets.varianceHint: Variances are positive when better than planned: income above budget, or expenses below it.
budgets.newBody: A plan for a financial year’s income and expenses, by month.
budgets.adjustHint: For example 10 for ten per cent more, or -5 for less.

errors.name_taken: This year already has a budget with that name.
errors.not_pnl_account: Budgets are for income and expense accounts.
errors.forbidden: You don’t have permission to change budgets.
errors.generic: The budget couldn’t be saved. Try again.

budgets.costCentreHint: A plan for one cost centre or project is compared with its lines only.

costCentres.title: Cost centres and projects
costCentres.description: The departments, branches and projects you tag lines with, to see profit for each part of the business.
costCentres.emptyBody: Add a department, branch or project, then tag journal, invoice and bill lines with it.
costCentres.deleteBody: Only a cost centre nothing has been tagged with can be deleted. Archive it to stop using it.
costCentres.dialogBody: Tag lines with it to see profit for this part of the business.
costCentres.codeHint: Short and unique, e.g. PUNE or PRJ-ALPHA
costCentres.codeInvalid: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores.

errors.code_taken: Another cost centre has this code.
errors.in_use: Lines are tagged with this cost centre. Archive it instead.
errors.cost_centre_archived: That cost centre is archived. Choose another, or restore it.
errors.forbidden: You don’t have permission to change cost centres.
errors.generic: The cost centre couldn’t be saved. Try again.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.description: What’s in stock and what it’s worth at average cost, how each item moved, and adjustments.
inventory.emptyBody: Turn on stock tracking for a goods item to keep its quantity on hand here.
inventory.trackHint: Keep the quantity on hand: bills bring it in, invoices take it out at average cost to cost of sales.
inventory.adjustBody: Count stock in (opening stock, found) or out (damaged, lost, used in-house). The value goes to the account you choose.
inventory.unitCostHint: Leave empty to use the current average cost.

problems.quantity: Enter a quantity above zero, with up to 4 decimal places.

errors.insufficient_stock: Not enough in stock: only {{onHand}} on hand.
errors.stock_used: Some of this stock has been sold or written off since, so it can’t go back.
errors.account_invalid: Choose another account for the other side.
errors.unit_cost_required: There’s none in stock to take the cost from. Enter what one cost.
errors.already_undone: This adjustment has already been undone.
errors.stock_moved: This item has stock movements, so its stock tracking and inventory account can’t change now.
errors.not_goods: Only goods have stock to track.
errors.inventory_account_required: Choose the inventory account the stock sits in.
errors.cogs_account_required: Choose the cost of sales account stock goes to as it sells.
errors.inventory_account_type: Stock sits in an asset account.
errors.cogs_account_type: The cost of stock sold goes to an expense account.
errors.in_use: Invoices, bills or stock movements use this item. Archive it instead.

inventory.reorderHint: Marked low when stock falls to this or below. Leave empty for none.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.description: A second pair of eyes before money moves: entries, bills and payments over a limit wait here for someone else’s yes.
approvals.nothingPendingBody: Entries, bills and payments held by a rule appear here.
approvals.approveBody: It posts now, under your name.
approvals.sendBackBody: It stays as it is; the person who sent it sees your note and can change it and send it again.
approvals.rulesBody: Documents at or above an amount wait for someone other than the person who sent them.
approvals.rulesReadOnly: Set by the organisation’s owners and admins.

rules.bank_spend: Money spent from the bank needs approval

approvals.sent: Sent for approval. It posts once someone approves it.
approvals.alreadyWaiting: This is already waiting for approval.

errors.own_request: Someone else has to approve what you sent.
errors.already_decided: Someone has already decided on this.
errors.document_changed: It has changed since it was sent. Send it back so it can be sent again.
errors.document_gone: It’s no longer a draft, so there’s nothing to approve.
errors.not_yours: Only the person who sent it can withdraw it.
errors.forbidden: You don’t have permission to decide on approvals.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.hint: Receipts, PDFs or photos up to 2 MB each, ten at most.

errors.type_mismatch: That file isn’t the type it claims to be.
errors.too_many: Keep it to ten files per document.
errors.wrongType: Attach a PDF, PNG, JPEG or WebP file.
errors.generic: The file couldn’t be attached. Try again.

imports.title: Import
imports.description: Bring your existing books in from a spreadsheet. Every row is checked before anything is saved.

about.accounts: Code, name and type for each account (asset, liability, equity, income or expense), with a sub-type and a parent code if it’s a sub-account.
about.contacts: A row per customer or vendor: name, whether they’re a customer, vendor or both, and any GSTIN, email, address and payment terms.
about.items: Products and services with their prices, HSN or SAC code and the codes of the accounts they post to.
about.opening_balances: Each account’s balance on the day you start: a debit or a credit per row. They become one draft journal entry to look over and post; any difference goes to Opening balance equity.

imports.chooseFile: Choose a CSV or Excel file
imports.matchBody: We guessed from the headers; change any that are wrong. Fields marked * are needed.
imports.sample: The first rows, as they’ll be read
imports.checkFirst: Check the rows first: nothing is saved until every one is right.
imports.someWrong: {{bad}} of {{count}} rows need fixing. Correct them in the file and choose it again, or change the columns.
imports.allRight: All {{count}} rows are right. Import them when you’re ready.
imports.openingDifference: The difference of {{amount}} goes to Opening balance equity.
imports.empty: The file has no rows under its headers.
imports.tooMany: Import up to {{max}} rows at a time.
imports.unreadable: That file couldn’t be read. Save it as CSV or XLSX and try again.
imports.notSaved: Nothing was saved: some rows need fixing.
imports.openingDone: Opening balances saved as a draft entry
imports.noPermission: You don’t have permission to import anything here.

tally.title: Move from Tally
tally.body: In Tally, open Display More Reports › List of Accounts, export it as XML, and choose the file here. Your ledgers become accounts, Sundry Debtors and Creditors become customers and vendors (with GSTIN, address and credit days), and the opening balances go into a draft entry to check.
tally.noLedgers: No ledgers were found in that file. Export the List of Accounts as XML from Tally.
tally.partyNote: Customer and vendor balances go to the Debtors and Creditors accounts as totals; any difference goes to Opening balance equity. Check the draft entry before posting it.
tally.stopped: The import stopped: fix the file and try again.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Let other systems call LedgerNest with an API key, and tell them when invoices, payments and bills change.
integrations.demoNote: In the demo nothing leaves your browser: keys can’t be used, and test events are only recorded.

keys.title: API keys
keys.body: A key acts for you, within the scopes you choose, and never does more than you can.
keys.madeBody: This is the only time it’s shown. Keep it somewhere safe, like a password.
keys.howTo: Send it as “Authorization: Bearer <key>” to the API. It works in this organisation only.
keys.revokeBody: Whatever uses it stops working at once. This can’t be undone.
keys.newBody: Name it after what will use it, and choose what it may do.
keys.name: Name
keys.scopesHint: Only what you can do yourself is offered.

hooks.title: Webhooks
hooks.body: LedgerNest posts to these addresses when something happens, retrying for up to half a day if they don’t answer.
hooks.verify: Each request is a JSON POST with X-LedgerNest-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "t.body" with this secret, in hex>. Check it, and that t is recent, before trusting the body.
hooks.removeBody: Nothing more is sent there, and its delivery log goes too.
hooks.newBody: The address LedgerNest should post to, and which events it wants.
hooks.badUrl: Use an https:// address that isn’t on a private network.

scheduledReports.title: Scheduled reports
scheduledReports.body: Reports made weekly or monthly, kept here and emailed to the people you choose.
scheduledReports.emptyBody: Have the month’s profit and loss, or who owes what, arrive by itself.
scheduledReports.ranEmailed: Report made and emailed to {{count}} people
scheduledReports.removeBody: No more will be made, and the files already made go too.
scheduledReports.recipientsFailed: It couldn’t be scheduled: check the recipients can see reports.
scheduledReports.newBody: It’s made for the period just ended, kept here, and emailed when email is set up.

periodHint.weekly: Each week covers the seven days before the day it’s made.
periodHint.monthly: Each month covers the calendar month before; balances are as of its last day.

scheduledReports.recipientsHint: Only members who can see reports receive them.

backups.title: Backups
backups.body: Download all of this organisation’s books as one file, and restore a file as a new organisation you own. People, API keys and the audit trail stay behind.
backups.bodyDemo: Download everything the demo keeps in this browser, and put a file back in its place.
backups.restoredDemo: The demo company now holds the file’s data
backups.tooBig: That file is too big to restore here.
backups.restored: {{name}} is ready: choose it from your organisations.
backups.restoreBody: It’s checked first, then restored as a new organisation with you as its owner. This organisation isn’t touched.
backups.restoreBodyDemo: The demo company’s data in this browser is replaced by the file’s.

quotes.title: Quotes
quotes.description: Estimates for customers, priced like invoices. Accepted ones become invoices in one step.
quotes.search: Search by number, customer or reference
quotes.emptyBody: Send a customer a price before you invoice: same lines, same GST.
quotes.expiryHint: Open for {{days}} days unless you choose a date
quotes.deleteBody: It goes for good. Quotes that have been sent stay; decline them instead.
quotes.newHint: Choose the customer and lines; GST works out as it does on invoices.

errors.not_editable: Only draft and sent quotes can change.
errors.not_draft: Only draft quotes can be deleted. Decline it instead.
errors.bad_move: The quote can’t move that way.
errors.already_invoiced: This quote is already an invoice.
errors.declined: A declined quote can’t be invoiced. Mark it accepted first.
errors.not_sendable: Only open or accepted quotes can be emailed.
errors.mail_off: Email isn’t set up on this server. Print the quote and send it yourself.
errors.no_email: This customer has no email address. Enter one to send it to.
errors.mail_failed: The email couldn’t be sent. Try again later.

email.title: Email {{number}} to the customer
email.body: It goes as a PDF with the lines, totals and valid-until date.
email.bodyDraft: It goes as a PDF with the lines, totals and valid-until date, and the quote is marked sent.
email.sentDemo: In the demo nothing is really sent; it would go to {{email}}

share.title: Share quote {{number}}
share.description: A link your customer opens without an account, to see the quote, download it and accept or decline. Sharing a draft marks it sent.
share.message: Dear {{name}}, here is quote {{number}} from {{organization}} for {{amount}}. You can see it and accept it here: {{link}}
share.acceptedBy: Accepted by {{name}} from the quote link.
share.declinedBy: Declined by {{name}} from the quote link.

emailDialog.noteHint: Optional: it goes at the top of the email.

recurringBills.title: Recurring bills
recurringBills.description: Rent, subscriptions and other bills that come every month or year, made from a template as they fall due.
recurringBills.emptyBody: Open a bill and choose Make recurring.
recurringBills.autoRecord: Record each bill as it’s made
recurringBills.autoRecordHint: Otherwise each one waits as a draft to check. An approval rule may still hold it.
recurringBills.deleteBody: It goes for good. Schedules that have made bills can only be paused.

publicInvoice.askBusiness: Ask the business that sent it for a new link.
publicInvoice.tryAgain: Check your connection and try again.
publicInvoice.upiBody: Scan with any UPI app, or tap the button on your phone. The amount and invoice number are filled in.
publicInvoice.upiAfter: The money goes straight to the business’s bank account. It can take them a little while to mark the invoice paid.

forgot.title: Reset your password
forgot.body: Enter the email you sign in with. We’ll send a link to choose a new password.
forgot.sentBody: If {{email}} has a LedgerNest account, a reset link is on its way. It works for {{minutes}} minutes.

reset.title: Choose a new password
reset.body: After this, every device signed in to your account is signed out.
reset.doneBody: Sign in with your new password. Other devices have been signed out.
reset.badLinkBody: Reset links work once, for a short time. Ask for a new one.

change.title: Change your password
change.description: Other devices signed in to your account will be signed out; this one stays signed in.
change.done: Password changed. Other devices have been signed out.

everywhere.title: Sign out of every device?
everywhere.body: Every browser and phone signed in to your account, this one too, will need to sign in again. Use it if you think someone else has your password.

errors.same: Choose a password different from the current one.

password.demo: In the demo there are no real passwords, so nothing changed and no email was sent.

page.title: Something went wrong on this page
page.body: Your data is safe: nothing was saved halfway. Reload to try again, or go back to the dashboard.
page.newVersion: A new version of LedgerNest came out while this tab was open. Reload to get it.
page.notFoundBody: The address may have a typo, or the page has moved. Everything is reachable from the menu.

tally.title: For your accountant: Tally Prime
tally.body: If your CA keeps your books in Tally, give them these two files. Your accounts, customers and vendors become Tally ledgers under its own groups; each posted entry becomes a voucher (sales, purchases, receipts, payments, contra, journals).
tally.step1: Ledgers first: in Tally, Gateway of Tally → Import → Masters.
tally.step2: Then the vouchers for the dates: Import → Transactions.
tally.failed: The Tally file couldn’t be made. Try again.

debitNotes.title: Debit notes
debitNotes.description: Goods sent back to vendors and credits they gave, against their bills, and where the credit went.
debitNotes.createBody: Choose how much of each line goes back. Its input GST comes back off too, and the credit comes off the bill first.
debitNotes.stockLine: kept in stock: use a stock adjustment

fields.vendorReferenceHint: If the supplier sent one; it shows in GSTR-2B.

debitNotes.offBill: All of it comes off what the bill still has to be paid.
debitNotes.someLeftOver: {{amount}} is more than the bill has left: it stays as credit with the vendor.
debitNotes.emptyBody: Open a recorded bill and choose Debit note to send goods back or record a credit from the supplier.
debitNotes.applyBody: {{amount}} of credit left to put on another of the vendor’s bills.
debitNotes.refundBody: Record {{name}} paying the remaining credit back.
debitNotes.voidBody: Its entry is reversed today and the bills it went onto are owed again.

problems.amount: Check the amount: no more than the credit left or the bill’s balance.
problems.bank: Choose the account the refund came into.

errors.over_credited: That’s more than is left to send back on a line.
errors.line_not_found: A line isn’t on this bill.
errors.before_bill: A debit note can’t be dated before its bill.
errors.over_applied: That’s more credit than is left on this note.
errors.has_refunds: The vendor refunded some of this credit, so it can’t be voided.
errors.before_vendor_credit: A refund can’t be dated before its debit note.
errors.stock_line: Goods kept in stock go back with a stock adjustment instead.
errors.bill_currency: Debit notes are for bills in rupees for now.
errors.bill_not_open: Only recorded bills can be credited.

email.title: Email debit note {{number}}
email.body: The vendor gets the debit note as a PDF.
email.blankHint: Leave blank to use the vendor’s email address.
email.sentDemo: In the demo nothing is really sent; it would go to {{email}}
email.noEmail: This vendor has no email address. Enter one to send it to.

delete.title: Delete your account?
delete.body: Your name and email are erased and you can’t sign in again. What you recorded stays in the books, shown as a deleted user, as accounting records must be kept.
delete.soleOwner: You’re the only Owner of {{names}}. Make someone else Owner, or delete the organisation, first.
delete.lastSuperAdmin: You’re the only Super Admin. Make someone else Super Admin first.

customerAccount.msmeInterest: Interest for late payment under the MSMED Act, 2006 (section 16) so far: {{amount}}
customerAccount.statement: Download your statement for this year

twoFactor.title: Two-factor sign-in
twoFactor.body: Ask for a code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy…) as well as the password, so a stolen password isn’t enough.
twoFactor.isOff: Two-factor sign-in is off. Turn it on to protect your books.
twoFactor.codeOrRecovery: Code from the app, or a recovery code
twoFactor.scan: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
twoFactor.manual: Can’t scan it? Type this key into the app instead:
twoFactor.qrLabel: QR code to add LedgerNest to an authenticator app
twoFactor.codesBody: Keep these recovery codes somewhere safe. Each one signs you in once if you lose your phone. They won’t be shown again.

errors.code: That code isn’t right. Try the newest code from your app.

gate.title: Turn on two-factor sign-in
gate.body: {{organization}} asks everyone to sign in with a code from an authenticator app as well as their password. Set it up to continue.

sessions.title: Where you’re signed in
sessions.body: Each device or browser signed in to your account. Sign out any you don’t recognise, then change your password.

confirmations.title: Balance confirmations
confirmations.hint: For the audit: ask customers or vendors to confirm their balance with you on a date, usually the year end.
confirmations.askBodyReceivable: Every customer with a balance on {{date}} gets a link to agree or dispute it. Ask again later and the same links are used.
confirmations.askBodyPayable: Every vendor with a balance on {{date}} gets a link to agree or dispute it. Ask again later and the same links are used.
confirmations.emailHint: Those without an email address (or if email isn’t set up): share the link on WhatsApp from the list.
confirmations.nobody: No one on that side had a balance on that day.
confirmations.emptyTitle: No confirmations asked for this day
confirmations.emptyBody: Ask for confirmation to send each party their balance.
confirmations.whatsappReceivable: Dear {{name}}, for our audit please confirm your balance with us as on {{date}}: {{amount}}. Agree or tell us your figure here: {{url}}
confirmations.whatsappPayable: Dear {{name}}, for our audit please confirm our balance with you as on {{date}}: {{amount}}. Agree or tell us your figure here: {{url}}

confirmation.title: Balance confirmation
confirmation.dear: Dear {{name}}, for the audit of {{organization}}, please confirm your balance with us.
confirmation.question: Does this match your books?
confirmation.theirsHint: As the amount above shows it; leave blank if you’d rather explain.
confirmation.why: What differs (payments, invoices or notes not shown)
confirmation.name: Your name
confirmation.thanksDisputed: Thank you. {{name}} told us the balance differs; we’ll look into it.

errors.name: Enter your name.
errors.amount: Enter the amount as a number, like 1,00,000.
errors.why: Tell us your balance, or what differs.
errors.failed: That didn’t go through. Try again.

publicQuote.title: Quote {{number}}
publicQuote.name: Your name
publicQuote.accepted: Accepted by {{name}}. Thank you: the business will be in touch.
publicQuote.expired: This quote expired on {{date}}. Ask the business for a new one.

errors.name: Enter your name.
errors.closed: This quote can’t be answered any more.
errors.failed: That didn’t go through. Try again.

collections.title: Collections
collections.description: Customers with something overdue, the most first, to chase in a tap.
collections.summary_one: 1 customer owes {{amount}} past its due date.
collections.summary_other: {{count}} customers owe {{amount}} past their due dates.
collections.emptyBody: Every customer is paid up or within their terms.
collections.email: Email {{name}} a reminder for each overdue invoice
collections.message_one: Dear {{name}}, {{amount}} is overdue with {{organization}} (1 invoice, {{days}} days late). You can see it and pay by UPI here: {{link}}
collections.message_other: Dear {{name}}, {{amount}} is overdue with {{organization}} ({{count}} invoices, the oldest {{days}} days late). You can see them and pay the lot by UPI here: {{link}}

yearEnd.title: Year-end close
yearEnd.description: Everything to do before the books for the year are final and go to the auditor, in order.

details.drafts_one: 1 journal entry is still a draft.
details.confirmationsNone: Not asked yet: ask customers and vendors to confirm their year-end balances.
details.msme: {{amount}} owed past the deadline would be disallowed if still unpaid at the year end.
details.close_other: {{count}} months are still open. Closing the last one moves the year’s profit to retained earnings.
details.backup: Download a full backup from Settings and keep it safe; books must be kept for eight years.

address.pinHint: Enter the PIN code first: the state, city and area fill in from India Post.
address.pinInvalid: A PIN code is 6 digits, not starting with 0.
address.unknown: India Post doesn’t know this PIN code. Check it, or type the city and area.
address.unreachable: India Post couldn’t be reached. Type the city and area.

numbering.title: Number series
numbering.body: How invoices, credit notes and debit notes are numbered: a prefix and suffix around a running number, at most 16 characters as GST requires. A number is kept once given, so changes apply to the next document.
numbering.keptHint: Documents already numbered keep their numbers.
numbering.name: Name
numbering.tokens: Letters, digits, - and /. Add the year with {FY} (2026-27), {FY2} (26-27), {YYYY} or {YY}.
numbering.resetYearly: Start again from the first number each financial year
numbering.makeDefault: Use for new documents of this type
numbering.preview: The next number will look like

errors.name_taken: There is already a series with that name.
errors.too_long: Numbers would be longer than the 16 characters GST allows. Shorten the prefix or suffix.
errors.no_room: The start number has more digits than the series allows.
errors.default_needed: Make another series the default first.
errors.in_use: This series has numbered documents. Archive it instead.

batches.track: Keep in batches with expiry dates
batches.trackHint: For medicines, food and anything that expires: bills record each batch and its dates, sales take the earliest expiry first and never expired stock. Turn it on before any stock moves.

errors.batch_required: This item is kept in batches: enter the batch number.
errors.batch_dates_differ: That batch is already recorded with other dates. Check the batch number.
errors.batch_expired: That batch has expired and can’t be sold.
errors.insufficient_batch: There isn’t that much left in batch {{batch}}: {{onHand}} on hand.
errors.insufficient_unexpired: Only {{onHand}} in stock that hasn’t expired.
errors.batch_invalid: That batch isn’t one of the item’s.
errors.batches_need_stock: Only goods whose stock is tracked can be kept in batches.

expiring.title: Expiring stock
expiring.summary: {{expired}} batches expired ({{expiredValue}}), {{expiring}} expiring within {{days}} days ({{expiringValue}}). Sell the earliest first, and write off or return what has expired.
